Craig — thanks for the clear scenarios. Short answers up top: we bill based on actual used tokens (input + output) at 1-token granularity, but we also apply a small rounding quantum for streaming chunks and a conversation/session-level minimum in a few hosting SKUs. Below are worked examples and how KV-cache affects effective billable tokens.

Example A — Long-context analysis (single call):
- Payload: 25,000 input tokens (full doc) + 3,000 output tokens streamed back.
- Metering: Redwood charges input + output = 28,000 tokens. Billing = 28,000 tokens * per-token rate (no implicit charge for model max context).
- Rounding: For streamed output we round each issued chunk to the streaming quantum (configurable per route). Default quantum = 16 tokens for efficiency on hosted streaming. If your streaming client receives 3,000 tokens in 16-token chunks, rounding overhead is at most ~(16/streaming_chunk_count) negligible; we include that in examples below.
- Effective billed tokens (worst-case rounding): output rounding adds up to +~8 tokens on average (depends on chunking), so billed ≈ 28,008 tokens.

Example B — Repeated short streaming with KV-cache:
- Per call raw: 60 input + 120 output = 180 tokens.
- KV-cache: if a 40-token prefix is cached and reused, that 40-token portion of the input is not re-sent and does not count as billable input. We bill only the tokens transmitted to the model for that call (i.e., remaining 20 tokens + any un-cached context).
- Aggregation/aggregation windows: billing is per-token across invoice period (daily/monthly aggregation), not per-account-call rounding. Rounding quantum applies per-streamed chunk at the moment it's generated, not aggregated later.
- Example per-call billed tokens after cache: 20 input + 120 output ≈ 140 tokens; with streaming quantum rounding (~16-token chunks) this may round the output up by up to 8 tokens occasionally.

Packaging notes:
- Hosted API: good if you want flexible scaling and no commit. Rounding and streaming quanta exist and are documented per-route.
- Dedicated/Reserved: if 30% of traffic is long-context (25k-ish) and you expect 100M tokens/mo, Dedicated reserved capacity can reduce per-token cost and remove conversation-level minimums that sometimes apply to pay-as-you-go hosted burst classes.

I'll include this as a short doc (matrix) and loop in pricing for a recommended pilot package. If you want exact numbers using your current per-token rates, share your target price band and I can produce the spreadsheet rows.

Sean — attached is a compact pricing matrix and guidance for negotiation. High level recommendations below (pasteable rows are in draft-pricing-matrix.xlsx):

1) 3-line matrix rows (numbers use baseline hosted = $0.0004/token):
- Hosted baseline (pay-as-you-go): $0.0004/token. Example (Example A from Sean): 28,000 tokens * $0.0004 = $11.20 (hosted). Streaming rounding overhead worst case +$0.0032 (~0.03% of call) — negligible per-call but material at scale; include as separate column.
- Hosted (accounting streaming quantum): apply streaming quantum overhead of 16-token rounding on output. Example cost = (25,000 + 3,008) * $0.0004 ≈ $11.20 (rounded).
- Dedicated reserved (12-mo commit): typical discount schedule we can offer for committed spend: 12-mo at 15% off baseline ($0.00034/token) for 100–249M tokens; 22% off ($0.000312/token) for 250M+ (note: exact discounts tied to CPU/GPU mix and any auxiliary capacity). For 100M tokens at 15% discount, monthly effective = 100,000,000 * $0.00034 = $34,000/month (compare to $40,000 hosted).

2) KV-cache guidance: conservative modeling assumes 20% billable reduction on input tokens for repeated prompts; for worst-case budgeting use 15% to be safe. We can provide a small instrumentation run during the pilot to measure actual hit rates and update model.

3) Pilot concessions: agree to a 30-day capped pilot at $12k (hosted rate) if they sign an MSA and share usage telemetry. We can waive conversation-level minimums for the pilot and include a 60-day post-pilot evaluation window. This is standard pilot concession but requires legal approval; I'll draft the terms-summary.docx for legal sign-off.

4) Positioning/ask strategy: offer the pilot + a one-time 10% credit on first-month usage if we convert to a 12-mo commit within 45 days. For pricing negotiation, hold 18% as a near-term discount target at the 100M mark — don't go below 15% on a firm 12-mo commit.

I've attached the pricing matrix and sample usage rows (draft-pricing-matrix.xlsx, sample-usage-rows.jsonl). Let me know if you want me to populate the HubSpot deal and Docs.
